title.value: Solving Combinatorial Pricing Problems using Embedded Dynamic Programming Models
title.justification: The title of the paper explicitly states the focus on solving combinatorial pricing problems using dynamic programming models, as described in the content.
title.quote: Solving Combinatorial Pricing Problems using Embedded Dynamic Programming Models

analysis.description: This paper addresses the combinatorial pricing problem (CPP), a bilevel problem where the leader aims to maximize revenue by setting tolls on items, affecting the subset chosen by the follower to solve a combinatorial optimization problem. The authors reformulate CPP into a single-level problem using dynamic programming and apply cutting plane methods for solution, exploring two dynamic programming models: selection diagrams and decision diagrams. They demonstrate the performance of these models across various CPP specializations and comparison with traditional value function approaches.

type.justification: The paper primarily discusses theoretical frameworks and methodologies for solving CPP and does not focus on empirical data or practical experimentations as its main content.
type.quote: In this paper, we derive a single-level reformulation for the CPP by rewriting the follower’s problem as a longest path problem using a dynamic programming model, and then taking its dual and applying strong duality.
